questions.prompt: A project is best described as:

options.text: Temporary work to create a unique outcome with constraints

questions.explanation: Projects are temporary and outcome-oriented under time/cost/scope constraints.

wrongExplanations.a: BAU operations differ from projects. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Email is communication, not the definition. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Departments are ongoing structures. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

options.text: Specific, time-bound, and measurable about the outcome

questions.explanation: Clear objectives align teams and make success testable.

wrongExplanations.a: Vague goals create misalignment. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Objectives must be shared. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Evaluability is required. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

options.text: Clarifying who is Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, and Informed

questions.explanation: Role clarity reduces dropped work and duplicate effort.

wrongExplanations.a: Communication remains necessary. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Risks still need management. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Dependencies still exist. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

options.text: Uncontrolled expansion of work beyond agreements

questions.explanation: Unmanaged additions threaten time, cost, and quality. That distinction is central to applying the lesson correctly.

wrongExplanations.a: Scope changes have tradeoffs. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Risk ID is different. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Buffers are schedule/contingency tools. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

questions.prompt: When a stakeholder requests major new deliverables late, you should:

options.text: Silently absorb them with no discussion
Document impact and seek a decision on tradeoffs (scope/time/cost/quality)
Hide the request from the sponsor

questions.explanation: Change control turns surprises into explicit choices. That distinction is central to applying the lesson correctly.

wrongExplanations.a: Silent absorption creates failure modes. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Communication is the job. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Sponsors need visibility. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

questions.prompt: A work breakdown structure helps by:

options.text: Decomposing deliverables into manageable owned pieces

questions.explanation: Decomposition improves clarity, ownership, and estimating. That distinction is central to applying the lesson correctly.

wrongExplanations.a: Visibility is the point. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Milestones still help. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Estimates remain uncertain but improve. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

options.text: Tasks never wait on each other
One delayed predecessor can stall successors and the end date
They only exist in software projects

questions.explanation: Critical sequencing determines what actually moves the deadline.

wrongExplanations.a: Dependencies are common. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Every domain has dependencies. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Communication remains necessary. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

options.text: Likelihood, impact, owner, trigger, and response approach
No owner so everyone owns it
A promise that risks cannot happen

questions.explanation: Actionable risk management needs ownership and responses. That distinction is central to applying the lesson correctly.

wrongExplanations.a: Names alone do not manage risk. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Clear owners beat diffused ownership. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Risks can and do occur. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

options.text: Outcome confidence, blockers/asks, and what changed

questions.explanation: Leaders need decision-ready truth, not activity fog. That distinction is central to applying the lesson correctly.

wrongExplanations.a: Activity diaries hide outcomes. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Bad news early is valuable. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Late surprises destroy trust. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

questions.explanation: Testable criteria reduce end-game arguments. That distinction is central to applying the lesson correctly.

wrongExplanations.a: Vibes are not verifiable. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Criteria guide building before launch. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Teams need shared definitions. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

quizzes.title: Final Quiz — Project Judgment
quizzes.intro: Apply foundations to realistic delivery decisions.

questions.prompt: “Launch a better onboarding process” should become:

options.text: A measurable objective with scope, date, and success metric

questions.explanation: Precision turns wishes into manageable projects. That distinction is central to applying the lesson correctly.

wrongExplanations.a: Vagueness causes misalignment. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Projects need endings and metrics. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Risks support, but do not replace objectives. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

questions.prompt: If design is done but development slips, the PM should:

options.text: Hide the slip until launch day
Communicate impact early and present options

questions.explanation: Early honesty enables tradeoff decisions. That distinction is central to applying the lesson correctly.

wrongExplanations.a: Hiding slips destroys trust. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Public blame harms culture. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Plans should be updated, not deleted. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

options.text: Practical reviews of what to repeat and change next time
Skipped because teams are tired always

questions.explanation: Closeout learning compounds organizational capability. That distinction is central to applying the lesson correctly.

wrongExplanations.a: Blame blocks learning. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Tiredness is why short structured closeout matters. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Write learning down. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

questions.prompt: Choosing agile vs predictive approaches should depend on:

options.text: Uncertainty, requirement stability, and coordination needs

questions.explanation: Method fit follows context, not ideology. That distinction is central to applying the lesson correctly.

wrongExplanations.a: Buzzwords are not criteria. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Stakeholders remain central. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Acceptance criteria remain useful. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

questions.prompt: Mature project management is mainly about:

options.text: Creating clarity and coordination around temporary work

questions.explanation: Clarity, coordination, and adaptive control are the craft.

wrongExplanations.a: Micromanagement is not the goal. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Meetings should earn their time. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
